Explain what each of the different parts are for, including the fuselage, wings, tail and engines. Write 150-200 words. Response: An airplane consists of several key parts that work together to ensure it can fly safely and efficiently. The fuselage is the main body of the airplane, providing space for passengers, cargo, and the cockpit where the pilots control the aircraft. It also serves as a structural frame that holds the other parts in place.

The wings are crucial for flight. They generate lift by moving air faster over the top surface than the bottom, creating an upward force that allows the plane to stay in the air. The shape and angle of the wings are carefully designed to provide the most efficient lift.

The tail of the airplane, also known as the empennage, consists of the horizontal stabilizer and the vertical stabilizer. The horizontal stabilizer helps to keep the plane level and prevent pitching, while the vertical stabilizer controls the plane’s yaw, or side-to-side movement.

Finally, the engines provide the thrust needed for the airplane to move forward. Most commercial airplanes use jet engines that take in air, compress it, mix it with fuel, and then expel it at high speed to propel the aircraft forward.

Each of these parts works together to ensure the airplane can fly smoothly and safely.

Despite its controversies, NAFTA played a pivotal role in shaping North American trade relations and global economic dynamics for over two decades.

The primary goal of NAFTA was to eliminate trade barriers and facilitate the free flow of goods and services among the three countries. By reducing tariffs and other trade restrictions, NAFTA aimed to boost economic growth and strengthen economic ties within North America.

NAFTA had several key objectives, including the reduction of trade barriers, the creation of trade rules, the improvement of working conditions, and the establishment of a safe market for North American goods and services. The agreement particularly focused on sectors such as agriculture, automotive, and textiles, gradually phasing out tariffs on these products12.

Despite its benefits, NAFTA faced criticism and controversy. Some argued that it led to job losses in certain industries due to increased competition, while others believed it contributed to economic growth and job creation overall. In 2020, NAFTA was replaced by the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA), which aimed to modernize and address the shortcomings of the original agreement12.

Overall, NAFTA played a crucial role in shaping trade relations in North America and set the stage for future trade agreements.

These narratives frequently explore identity and the sacrifices made in the pursuit of dreams or love. Moreover, mermaids have become symbols of environmental awareness, representing the need to protect our oceans and marine life. Their enduring presence in popular culture underscores a timeless allure that bridges fantasy with real-world issues, inviting audiences to ponder the depths of both the sea and the human spirit.</input>

text_a: Prompt Level: 7.0 Prompt: Write a summary of the disadvantages of the following modes of research: focus group, survey and interview. Compare your text with the model. This is a non-graded activity. Response: nan
text_b: Disadvantages of Different Research Methods Focus Group Dominance of Strong Opinions: More vocal participants may dominate the discussion, influencing others' responses and skewing results. Groupthink: Participants may conform to group opinions rather than expressing their true thoughts. Limited Generalizability: Small sample sizes reduce the ability to generalize findings to a larger population. Moderator Bias: The facilitator’s approach and wording can unintentionally influence responses. Logistical Challenges: Scheduling and managing diverse participants can be complex and time-consuming. Survey Limited Depth: Responses are often superficial, lacking detailed explanations or personal context. Low Response Rates: Many potential respondents ignore surveys, leading to incomplete data. Misinterpretation of Questions: Without clarification, respondents may misunderstand questions, leading to inaccurate answers. Self-Selection Bias: People who choose to respond may not be representative of the broader population. Rigid Structure: Fixed answer choices may not fully capture participants' true thoughts or experiences. Interview Time-Consuming: Conducting and analyzing individual interviews takes considerable time and effort. Interviewer Bias: The interviewer’s tone, body language, or phrasing may unintentionally influence responses. High Costs: One-on-one interviews require significant resources, especially for large sample sizes. Limited Sample Size: Due to time and resource constraints, fewer participants can be interviewed, reducing generalizability. Potential Dishonesty: Participants may alter their responses based on social desirability or perceived expectations. Each method has its strengths, but these limitations should be considered when choosing the best approach for a research project.

text_b: Counterfeit goods are products that are made and sold with the intent to deceive consumers by imitating authentic brands. These illicit items can be found across various categories, including luxury fashion (handbags, shoes, and watches), electronics (phones and accessories), pharmaceuticals (medications), and even food and beverages (spirits and cosmetics). The proliferation of counterfeit goods is a growing concern, affecting not only consumers but also legitimate businesses and the economy as a whole. The impact of counterfeiting on society is profound. It leads to significant financial losses for businesses, resulting in fewer jobs and reduced tax revenues. Moreover, counterfeit products often come with safety and health risks, particularly in categories like pharmaceuticals, where fake medications can jeopardize lives. This undermines trust in genuine brands and hampers innovation. Identifying counterfeit goods can be challenging. However, there are key signs to look out for: unusually low prices, poor quality materials, misspellings or inaccuracies in branding, and lack of proper labeling or certifications. Authentic products typically come with warranty information and detailed product packaging, which are frequently absent in fakes. If you discover counterfeit goods, it's important to take action. Report your findings to local authorities and consumer protection agencies, as they play a crucial role in combating counterfeiting. While returns can often be made through the vendor, it's advisable to keep receipts and document the item in question for evidence. By being informed and vigilant, consumers can help curb the spread of counterfeit goods and support genuine businesses in our communities.

text_b: The North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) The North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) was a landmark trade agreement signed by Canada, Mexico, and the United States, which came into effect on January 1, 1994. The primary goal of NAFTA was to eliminate trade barriers and facilitate the free flow of goods and services across the borders of the three member countries. Key Objectives: Elimination of Tariffs: NAFTA aimed to gradually eliminate tariffs on most goods traded between the member countries, making products more affordable and boosting trade. Market Access: The agreement provided better access to markets for businesses in all three countries, encouraging investment and economic growth. Protection of Intellectual Property: NAFTA included provisions to protect intellectual property rights, ensuring that creators and businesses could safeguard their innovations and creations. Dispute Resolution Mechanisms: The agreement established mechanisms for resolving trade disputes, promoting fair and transparent trade practices. Impact: NAFTA significantly increased trade and investment among the member countries. It created one of the largest free trade zones in the world, benefiting various industries such as automotive, agriculture, and manufacturing. However, it also faced criticism for its impact on labor markets and the environment. In 2020, NAFTA was replaced by the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA), which aimed to modernize and address the shortcomings of the original agreement.

Sreeja

text_b: **Understanding NAFTA: A Key Trade Agreement** The North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), established in 1994, was a trade deal between the United States, Canada, and Mexico. Its primary aim was to eliminate tariffs on goods traded between these three countries, promoting economic growth by increasing trade and investment. NAFTA created one of the world’s largest free trade zones, contributing significantly to the economies of all member nations. Under NAFTA, businesses had greater access to markets across North America. It allowed for the seamless flow of goods, services, and labor across borders, benefiting industries like agriculture, manufacturing, and automotive. The agreement also helped to lower prices for consumers by encouraging competition and innovation. However, NAFTA also faced criticism. Some argued that it led to job losses in certain sectors, particularly in manufacturing, as companies relocated to countries with lower labor costs. Environmental and labor rights groups raised concerns about the impact of the agreement on worker conditions and environmental regulations. In 2020, NAFTA was replaced by the **United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA)**, which updated several provisions, including intellectual property protections, labor rights, and environmental standards. Despite changes, the core purpose of enhancing trade between the three countries remains intact.

text_b: The North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) was a landmark trade pact signed by Canada, Mexico, and the United States. It came into effect on January 1, 1994, creating one of the world’s largest free trade zones. NAFTA aimed to eliminate most tariffs and trade barriers between the three countries, fostering increased trade and economic integration12. The agreement was negotiated by the administrations of U.S. President George H.W. Bush, Canadian Prime Minister Brian Mulroney, and Mexican President Carlos Salinas de Gortari. It built upon the earlier Canada-United States Free Trade Agreement of 1988, extending its provisions to Mexico12. NAFTA’s main provisions included the gradual reduction of tariffs, customs duties, and other trade barriers over a period of up to 15 years. This ensured duty-free access for a wide range of goods and services, promoting economic growth and job creation in all three countries2. Despite its benefits, NAFTA faced criticism for its impact on certain industries and workers exposed to trade competition. NAFTA aimed to eliminate trade barriers and tariffs, fostering a trilateral trade bloc in North America. As one of the largest free trade zones in the world, it sought to increase economic integration and cross-border trade among the member countries.

NAFTA significantly impacted the economies of the three nations. It facilitated the flow of goods and services, allowing for the reduction of costs associated with import and export processes. This resulted in expanded markets for businesses and consumers, leading to increased competitiveness and economic growth. However, it also faced criticism for contributing to job losses in certain sectors, particularly in manufacturing, as companies relocated production to countries with lower labor costs.

In 2020, NAFTA was replaced by the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA), which built upon its predecessor's framework while addressing contemporary issues such as digital trade, labor rights, and environmental protections. Despite its controversial aspects, NAFTA played a crucial role in shaping economic relationships and trade policies in North America for over two decades.

Ask yourself guiding questions to help organize the writing. Type in the input box. Write 150-250 words. Response: Issues and Challenges Language Students Often Face

Why is learning a new language difficult for many students? One major challenge is mastering pronunciation and listening skills. Different sounds, accents, and speech speeds can confuse learners, especially when they differ significantly from their native language.

Another issue is vocabulary retention. How can students remember hundreds or thousands of new words? Without regular practice, new vocabulary is quickly forgotten. Grammar rules add another layer of complexity. Why are grammar rules so frustrating? Because they often include many exceptions and may not match the student’s native language structure.

What about confidence? Many students fear making mistakes in front of others. This fear of embarrassment can stop them from speaking, even if they know the correct words. Motivation is another challenge. Why do some students give up? Progress may seem slow, especially without immediate rewards or real-life practice.

Finally, lack of exposure is a common problem. Without daily interaction in the language, it’s hard to develop fluency. Watching shows, talking to native speakers, or traveling can help—but not everyone has those opportunities.

In summary, language learners face difficulties with pronunciation, grammar, vocabulary, confidence, motivation, and exposure. Overcoming these requires consistent practice, patience, and the right learning environment.

Response: An airplane is made up of several key parts, each playing an essential role in flight.

    Fuselage: The fuselage is the main body of the aircraft. It contains the cockpit, where the pilots sit, and the cabin, where passengers or cargo are placed. It also connects all the other parts of the plane.

    Wings: The wings generate lift, which allows the plane to fly. Their special shape, called an airfoil, creates a pressure difference as air flows above and below them, pushing the plane upward. The wings also house the fuel tanks of most aircraft.

    Tail : The tail helps stabilize and steer the aircraft. It generally includes the horizontal stabilizer, which prevents the plane from tipping forward or backward, and the vertical stabilizer, which keeps the plane steady from side to side. The rudder and elevators on the tail allow pilots to control direction and pitch.

    Engines: Engines provide the thrust needed to propel the aircraft forward. Most modern airplanes use jet engines that produce powerful force by expelling air at high speeds.

Wings: The wings generate lift, which allows the plane to fly. Their special shape, called an airfoil, creates a pressure difference as air flows above and below them, pushing the plane upward. The wings also house the fuel tanks of most aircraft. Tail : The tail helps stabilize and steer the aircraft. It generally includes the horizontal stabilizer, which prevents the plane from tipping forward or backward, and the vertical stabilizer, which keeps the plane steady from side to side. The rudder and elevators on the tail allow pilots to control direction and pitch. Engines: Engines provide the thrust needed to propel the aircraft forward. Most modern airplanes use jet engines that produce powerful force by expelling air at high speeds.

Prompt Level: 11.0 Prompt: Read the blog about a law in Japan, then write about a law in your country. Type in the input box. Write 60-90 words. Use your own words where possible. Response: India has a vast and complex legal system with numerous laws covering various aspects of life. One of the most significant laws in India is the Right to Information Act, 2005 (RTI Act). This legislation is pivotal in promoting transparency and accountability in the functioning of the government.

**Right to Information Act, 2005**

**Overview:**
The Right to Information Act was enacted by the Parliament of India in June 2005 and came into force on October 12, 2005. The act is designed to empower citizens to seek information from public authorities, thereby promoting transparency and accountability in the workings of every public authority.

**Objectives:**
The main objectives of the RTI Act are to:

1. Ensure transparency and accountability in the functioning of public authorities.
2. Empower citizens to access information under the control of public authorities.
3. Promote openness and reduce corruption in government and its instrumentalities.

**Key Provisions:**
- **Right to Information:** Citizens have the right to request information from public authorities, which are required to reply expeditiously or within thirty days.
- **Public Authorities:** The act covers all constitutional authorities, including executive, judiciary, and legislature bodies, as well as any institution or body established by an act of Parliament or a state legislature.
- **Exemptions:** There are certain exemptions to the disclosure of information to protect national security, privacy, and other sensitive matters.
- **Procedure:** The act lays down a simple procedure for obtaining information. Citizens can file a request in writing or electronically, and the public authority is required to respond within a specified time frame.
- **Information Commissioners:** The act provides for the appointment of a Central Information Commission and State Information Commissions to handle appeals and complaints related to the RTI requests.

**Impact:**
The RTI Act has been instrumental in promoting transparency and accountability in government operations. It has empowered citizens to participate more actively in governance by enabling them to obtain information about public policies, decisions, and expenditures. The act has also played a significant role in uncovering corruption and maladministration.

**Challenges:**
Despite its success, the RTI Act faces several challenges, including:
- Delays in information dissemination due to bureaucratic hurdles.
- Lack of awareness among citizens about their rights under the act.
- Instances of harassment and threats to RTI activists.

Overall, the Right to Information Act, 2005, is a landmark legislation in India's legal framework, promoting greater transparency and accountability in the functioning of public authorities and enhancing the democratic process.

text_b: Understanding Counterfeit Goods Counterfeit goods are fake items that are made to look like genuine products. They cover a wide range of categories including luxury items (like designer clothing and handbags), electronics, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and even food and beverages. These fakes can be very convincing, making it challenging for consumers to differentiate between real and counterfeit products. Types of Counterfeit Goods Luxury Goods: High-end brands such as designer clothing, bags, watches, and jewelry. Electronics: Gadgets like smartphones, tablets, and accessories. Pharmaceuticals: Medicines and health supplements. Cosmetics: Beauty products, including makeup and skincare items. Food and Beverages: Packaged foods and alcoholic drinks. Effects of Counterfeiting on Society The impact of counterfeiting on society is profound and far-reaching. It undermines legitimate businesses, leading to significant revenue losses and job cuts. Counterfeit goods often fail to meet safety standards, posing serious health risks to consumers. For instance, fake pharmaceuticals can have life-threatening consequences. Additionally, the counterfeit trade is frequently linked to organized crime, funding illicit activities and contributing to broader societal issues like violence and corruption. Signs of a Fake Identifying counterfeit goods requires vigilance. Common signs include poor quality materials, misspelled brand names, and missing serial numbers or authenticity labels. Unusually low prices that seem too good to be true often signal fakes. Packaging that looks different from the original or lacks proper branding can also be a giveaway. What to Do If You Discover Fake Goods If you suspect that you have purchased counterfeit goods, report it immediately to the retailer and the brand owner. Avoid using the product, especially if it is a health-related item. Consumers can also report the incident to local consumer protection agencies and law enforcement authorities. Public awareness and swift reporting play crucial roles in combating the spread of counterfeit products.

The fuselage is the main body of the airplane, housing the cockpit, passenger seats, and cargo. The wings are crucial for generating lift, enabling the airplane to rise off the ground. They are designed with airfoils that create a pressure difference between the upper and lower surfaces, facilitating upward movement. Wings may also include control surfaces like ailerons and flaps to aid in maneuverability and stability during flight.

The tail, also known as the empennage, consists of the horizontal stabilizer and vertical stabilizer. The horizontal stabilizer helps maintain balance and control pitch, while the vertical stabilizer provides directional stability and houses the rudder, which is used for steering the airplane left or right.

Finally, the engines are the powerhouse of the airplane, providing thrust to propel it forward. Modern airplanes typically use jet engines, which are efficient and powerful, allowing for high-speed travel over long distances. Together, these parts work in harmony to ensure an airplane can fly safely and effectively.</input>

Subscribe Now Index dropdown-arrow HOME LOANS HOME LOANS HOME LOAN – MEANING, TYPES, ELIGIBILITY, AND FEATURES Home Loan – Meaning, Types, Eligibility, and Features Updated on: Jun 7th, 2024 | 3 min read Buying a house is one of the biggest dreams come true for most people and an extravagant affair altogether. Imparting life to such a dream requires a lot of effort from the buyers’ end and the best one can do to accommodate the home in their budget is through a home loan. A home loan can be opted to buy a new house/flat or a plot of land where you construct the house, and even for renovation, extension, and repairs to an existing house. Plan Early and Get ahead for next year’s savings Use Tax Calculator and get your taxes estimates in mins as per new budget Calculate Now Types of Home Loans in India Home Loan This is the most common type of home loan availed to purchase a house. There are many housing finance companies, public banks, and private banks that offer housing loans where you borrow money to purchase the house of your choice and repay the loan in monthly instalments. You can get up to 80%-90% of the house’s market price in the form of financing. The lender will hold the house until you completely repay the loan. Home Construction Loan This is the right home loan type if you already have a plot of land and you need financing to construct a house in that land. Home Extension Loan Say you already own a house and you would like to extend the house with another room or another floor to accommodate the growing family. Home extension loan provides financing for this purpose. Home Improvement Loan A home improvement loan provides financing for renovating or repairing the house if there’s any fault in the existing system, such as painting the house’s interior or exterior, plumbing, upgrading the electrical system, waterproofing the ceiling, and more. Home Loan Balance Transfer The current home loan interest rate may be overwhelming, or you may not be happy with your current lender’s service; you can transfer the home loan’s outstanding balance to a different lender who offers a lower interest rate and better service. Upon transfer, you can even check out the possibilities of a top-up loan on your existing one. Composite Home Loan This type of home loan provides financing for purchasing the plot of land where you would like to construct a house and for the construction, both within a single loan. Benefits of Taking a Home Loan Tax benefits The foremost benefit of a home loan is the income tax deduction you can claim on the interest and principal repayments. You can claim up to Rs.1.5 lakh on principal repayments u/s 80C, up to Rs.2 lakh on interest repayments u/s 24B, up to Rs.2 lakh on interest repayment in special circumstances u/s 80EE and 80EEA, and up to Rs.1.5 lakh on stamp duty expenses u/s 80C. Lower interest rate The home loan interest rate is much lower as compared to any other loan types available. If you come across a cash crunch, you may get a top-up on the existing home loan at a lower interest rate than a personal loan to solve the issue. Due diligence of property When you go through a bank to purchase a house, the bank will conduct thorough checks on the property from the legal perspective and check if all the documents produced are valid. This due diligence check from the bank’s end will reduce the risk of you being scammed. If the bank approves the property, that means you and your house are safe. Long repayment tenure Unlike any other loans, home loans come with longer repayment tenure, as much as 25-30 years. This is owing to the significant loan amount one will have to borrow to purchase a house. Spreading the loan amount and interest applicable over a longer tenure will reduce the monthly EMIs reducing the borrower’s burden.

<input>Corporate social responsibility (CSR) is a topic that sparks diverse opinions. I believe companies do have a responsibility to society, beyond just maximizing profits for shareholders. Here’s why:

Firstly, companies operate within communities that provide them with resources, labor, and a market for their products. It’s a symbiotic relationship where businesses benefit from the community, and in return, they should contribute positively to it. This can be through sustainable practices, fair wages, and community development projects. Such actions not only improve the quality of life for community members but also create a loyal customer base and a motivated workforce.

Secondly, CSR can be a strategic advantage. Consumers today are more informed and concerned about the ethical practices of the companies they support. A strong CSR program can enhance a company’s reputation, leading to increased customer loyalty and potentially higher profits. For instance, companies with good CSR records often find it easier to attract and retain talent, as employees prefer to work for organizations that align with their values.

However, it’s important to acknowledge the arguments against CSR. Critics argue that the primary responsibility of a business is to its shareholders and that CSR can sometimes be a superficial marketing tool. While there is some truth to this, genuine CSR efforts that are integrated into a company’s core strategy can lead to long-term benefits for both the business and society.

In conclusion, while the primary goal of a business is to generate profits, integrating CSR into its operations can create a win-win situation for both the company and the community. It’s about finding a balance where businesses can thrive while also contributing positively to society.</input>

Prompt Level: 7.0 Prompt: Your teacher has asked you to write a short text about the parts of an airplane. Explain what each of the different parts are for, including the fuselage, wings, tail and engines. Write 150-200 words. Response: An airplane is made up of several key parts, each with an important role in flight. The fuselage is the main body of the plane. It holds the passengers, cargo, and cockpit where the pilots sit. The wings are attached to the sides of the fuselage and are crucial for lift. As air flows over and under the wings, the difference in pressure helps the airplane rise into the sky.

At the back of the plane is the tail, also known as the empennage. The tail includes the vertical and horizontal stabilizers, which help keep the plane stable and balanced in the air. The rudder, located on the vertical stabilizer, controls left and right movement (yaw), while the elevator on the horizontal stabilizer controls up and down movement (pitch).

The engines, usually found under the wings or attached to the fuselage, provide the thrust needed to move the airplane forward. As the engines push the plane ahead, the wings generate lift, allowing it to fly. All these parts work together to ensure the aircraft flies safely and smoothly.

Use your own words where possible. Response: Subject lines are especially important if you're reaching out to someone for the first time. The recipient doesn't know who you are, and can only judge you from your subject line.

Even if you're sending emails internally at your company, it still pays to write a great subject line so your recipient has an idea of what to expect. Like any busy person, your teammates receive a ton of emails every day, and would certainly appreciate the extra effort of a descriptive subject line.

So, how do you write a good subject line?

Be clear, direct, and describe the content of your email. Don't be afraid to take up the whole subject line. Here are some great examples of subject lines.

[Action Required] Monthly Marketing Meeting
FYI/Informational
Request for [Insert here]
[Reminder] Survey to Complete | Will Take 2 Minutes
[Name] suggested I reach out to you
I'm going to be in town next Tues — are you available?
If you're sending a promotional email, avoid deceptive subject lines like:

RE:
FWD:
Urgent
Order confirmation
Account Status
There's no need to resort to sneaky tricks or clickbait titles just to induce an open. They make recipients feel cheated and tricked, according to a Litmus survey. You'll lose trust and may end up in their junk mail as a result.

You want to associate positive feelings with your email, not anger and disappointment.

If you are sending promotional emails or newsletters, we recommend that you test different subject lines with HubSpot's email marketing tools to see what works best for your audience. This can help you fine-tune your email strategy and improve your results over time

This positive image can lead to increased customer retention and attract new clients who value ethical considerations.

Secondly, CSR can lead to financial benefits. In conclusion, corporate social responsibility is not just a moral obligation but a strategic advantage. By integrating CSR into their core operations, companies can enhance their reputation, achieve financial gains, and create a positive impact on society. As consumers and stakeholders continue to demand ethical practices, businesses must recognize the importance of CSR and strive to make a meaningful difference.

text_a: Prompt Level: 15.0 Prompt: Apply the language you've learned in this lesson to a new topic: language learning. Write about issues and challenges that language students often face. Ask yourself guiding questions to help organize the writing. Type in the input box. Write 150-250 words. Response: nan
text_b:
<input>Language learning is a rewarding but often challenging journey. Students face a variety of obstacles that can hinder their progress. One major issue is lack of confidence—many learners fear making mistakes, which can prevent them from speaking or writing freely. This fear often stems from perfectionism or negative past experiences.

Another common challenge is limited exposure to the language outside the classroom. Without regular practice in real-life situations, it’s difficult to retain vocabulary and grammar. Learners may also struggle with pronunciation and listening comprehension, especially when native speakers talk quickly or use slang.

Motivation is another key factor. Language learning requires consistent effort over time, and students may lose interest if they don’t see immediate results. Additionally, differences in learning styles can affect progress—some students thrive with visual aids, while others prefer interactive or auditory methods.

To overcome these challenges, learners can ask themselves:

How can I create more opportunities to use the language daily?
What strategies help me remember new words or grammar rules?
How can I make learning more enjoyable and less stressful?
By identifying their personal obstacles and experimenting with different techniques, students can build confidence and make steady progress in their language journey.</input>

They are believed to reside in underground realms and are guardians of treasures and sacred places.

In Hindu mythology, Nagas are considered divine beings and are associated with water bodies like rivers, lakes, and oceans. They are revered for their wisdom and are often seen as protectors of nature. This is particularly challenging for those learning a language in a non-native environment, where opportunities to practice are limited.

Lastly, motivation plays a crucial role. Students who lack intrinsic motivation may find it hard to stay committed to their language studies, especially when progress seems slow. Balancing these challenges requires a supportive learning environment, diverse teaching methods, and ample opportunities for practice and cultural immersion.

Response: Buying a home and applying for a home loan in Brazil can be both exciting and challenging. The process typically starts by finding a suitable property, which can be done through real estate websites or with the help of a real estate agent. While using an agent isn’t mandatory, many people choose to work with one to navigate the paperwork and legal steps more easily.

Once you’ve found a home, applying for a mortgage—known locally as “financiamento imobiliário”—is the next step. This can be time-consuming, as banks and lenders require a lot of documentation. You must provide proof of income, identification, tax records, and sometimes a statement of assets. The bank will also assess your credit score and may require an initial down payment of around 20% of the property’s value.

Interest rates in Brazil have varied greatly over the years. As of 2025, rates tend to range between 9% and 12% per year, depending on the lender and the borrower’s profile. Compared to other countries, this is relatively high, making long-term financing more expensive.

Housing prices depend heavily on the city and neighborhood. In major cities like São Paulo or Rio de Janeiro, prices are high, especially in well-located areas. In smaller towns, homes are more affordable. Overall, the process requires patience, financial planning, and often professional help to avoid surprises.

Prompt Level: 11.0 Prompt: Write a paragraph about how media has changed in your lifetime. What media was important before? What do you use now, and how has it changed your reading habits? Pay attention to your use of commas, colons and semicolons. Type in the input box. Write 150-200 words. Use your own words where possible. Response: The media landscape has undergone dramatic changes over the past few decades, shaped by technological advancements, shifting consumer habits, and societal transformations. From the dominance of print newspapers to the rise of digital platforms, these changes have revolutionized how we create, consume, and interact with information.

1. Traditional to Digital
In the past, media was primarily distributed through newspapers, magazines, radio, and television. These formats followed a one-way communication model where media organizations produced content, and audiences consumed it passively. The internet disrupted this model, introducing digital media platforms that allow for instantaneous, global communication. Online publications, blogs, and social media have replaced much of the print industry, offering faster access to information and diverse perspectives.

2. The Rise of Social Media
Social media has transformed how we interact with media, making it more personal, participatory, and immediate. Platforms like Facebook, Twitter (now X), Instagram, and TikTok enable users to become content creators, bypassing traditional gatekeepers. This shift has democratized information but also introduced challenges, such as misinformation and the erosion of trust in reliable sources.

3. 24/7 News Cycle
The advent of cable news and later online news platforms introduced the 24/7 news cycle, drastically increasing the speed of reporting. While this provides timely updates, it also pressures media outlets to prioritize speed over depth, sometimes leading to inaccuracies or sensationalism.

Prompt Level: 16.0 Prompt: Write a criticism of a celebrity. It can be a particular celebrity or the whole idea of celebrity in general. Use some of the language you have learned for criticizing in this lesson. Type in the input box. Write 150-200 words. Response: Criticism towards a celebrity often focuses on their personal behavior, public statements, artistic choices, or perceived lack of authenticity, with common criticisms including: unprofessional conduct, hypocrisy, offensive remarks, poor decision-making, excessive self-promotion, unrealistic portrayals, and a disconnect from real-life issues; however, the nature of criticism can vary depending on the celebrity and the context of the situation. 
Key aspects of celebrity criticism:
Personal life:
Critics may scrutinize a celebrity's relationships, substance abuse issues, legal troubles, or family dynamics, sometimes considering their private life as a reflection of their character. 
Public image:
A celebrity's persona, particularly if perceived as carefully curated or inauthentic, can be a target for criticism, with accusations of being "too perfect" or not being true to themselves. 
Social and political stances:
When celebrities express strong opinions on social or political issues, they can face backlash from those who disagree with their views, especially if seen as opportunistic or uninformed. 
Artistic performance:
Actors, musicians, and other performers can be criticized for their acting skills, musical quality, or creative choices, with critiques focusing on technical aspects or the overall artistic direction. 
Impact on society:
Some criticism focuses on the potential negative influence a celebrity might have on their fans, particularly regarding body image, consumerism, or unhealthy behaviors. 
Examples of celebrity criticism:
"Cancel culture":
A recent trend where celebrities face intense public backlash and potential career consequences for past actions or statements considered offensive or harmful. 
"Unrealistic portrayals":
Actors might be criticized for perpetuating unrealistic beauty standards or lifestyle expectations through their roles. 
"Hypocrisy":
When a celebrity promotes a certain lifestyle or ethical values while engaging in behavior that contradicts those values. 
Important considerations:
Privacy concerns:
While celebrities often put themselves in the public eye, there are limits to what aspects of their personal life should be subject to criticism. 
Constructive criticism:
Criticism can be valuable when it focuses on specific areas of improvement or raises important issues, rather than simply being personal attacks. 
Media bias:
The way the media portrays a celebrity can influence public perception and sometimes lead to unfair or exaggerated criticism.

<input>Here’s a summary of the disadvantages of focus groups, surveys, and interviews:

Focus groups can be influenced by dominant participants, which may lead to biased opinions and limit the diversity of views. They also require careful moderation and can be time-consuming and costly to organize.

Surveys often suffer from low response rates, which can affect the reliability of the results. They may also limit the depth of information gathered due to fixed questions and lack of opportunity for follow-up.

Interviews, while providing detailed insights, can be time-consuming and expensive to conduct, especially if many participants are involved. Interviewer bias and the skill of the interviewer can also impact the quality of the data collected.

Each method has its limitations, so choosing the right one depends on the research goals, resources, and the type of information needed.</input>

Prompt Level: 7.0 Prompt: Your teacher has asked you to write a short text about the parts of an airplane. Explain what each of the different parts are for, including the fuselage, wings, tail and engines. Write 150-200 words. Response: An airplane consists of several key parts, each playing a crucial role in its operation.

Fuselage: The fuselage is the main body of the airplane, providing structural support and housing the cockpit, passenger cabin, and cargo space. It connects all other components and ensures the aircraft's integrity during flight.

Wings: Wings are essential for generating lift, allowing the airplane to rise into the air. They are designed with an airfoil shape, which helps create a difference in air pressure above and below the wing as the airplane moves forward. This lift is vital for takeoff and landing.

Tail: The tail section, or empennage, stabilizes the airplane and includes the horizontal stabilizer and vertical fin. The horizontal stabilizer helps control the pitch (up and down movement), while the vertical fin aids in controlling the yaw (side-to-side movement). Together, they enhance stability and maneuverability.

Engines: The engines provide the thrust needed to propel the airplane forward. They can be located on the wings or the fuselage and work by expelling exhaust gases to push the aircraft forward, allowing it to overcome drag and achieve flight.

text_b: NAFTA is a regional trade agreement among the countries of North America. The US, Canadaand Mexico are the member states. It has had a profound effect on trade relations. NAFTA began operating in 1994 following lengthy negotiations for an agreement between the United States, Mexico, and Canada. NAFTA's supporters were motivated by the success of the European Economic Community (EEC), which had led to the removal of trade barriers and customs duties, creating effective economic freedom among members. NAFTA was unique in that it brought together three countries with diverse organizations and economies. Its objectives were to: - Reduce or eliminate trade barriers and regulations between members. - Improve cooperation across North America by ensuring collaborative and mutually beneficial policies. - Encourage free tradeand provide a model for other states to follow. - Support and promote business operations across borders. Since its inception, NAFTA has tripled trade between the United States, Canada, and Mexico. It has also fostered economic growth and business development, as well as job creation and strengthening, including improvements to labor laws across the board. However, despite the economic benefits of this agreement, several drawbacks also emerged: - Loss of manufacturing jobs as some employers moved across borders to lower wages. - Negative impact on Mexican farmers and small business owners who could not compete with lower retail prices. - Laws and restrictions were not strict enough, and the growth had adverse environmental effects. - Stagnant wages and loss of benefits as companies threatened to relocate. In conclusion, NAFTA significantly reduced tariff barriers, facilitating trade in goods, services, and capital between the United States, Canada, and Mexico. This trade agreement created one of the largest free trade areas in the world. But despite its economic prospects, it was a source of concern from its inception: Americans and Canadians saw it as competition from Mexican labor, while Mexicans feared U.S. influence. Highly critical of it, US President Donald Trump sought to end it, calling NAFTA "the worst agreement ever signed." On November 30, 2018, the leaders of the three countries involved signed a new agreement, the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). Among the points negotiated (dairy products, intellectual property, etc.), the USMCA stipulates that the automotive industry must comply with rules governing the supply of American materials and components, and that Mexico must increase the wages of employees in this sector. Importantly, the agreement includes an entire chapter on digital technology, to regulate the expansion of GAFAM. Scheduled to enter into force in 2020 and run until 2036 and renewable once, the agreement will be subject to review every six years.

text_a: Prompt Level: 7.0 Prompt: Your teacher has asked you to write a short text about the parts of an airplane. Explain what each of the different parts are for, including the fuselage, wings, tail and engines. Write 150-200 words. Response: nan
text_b: Airplanes are extremely complex machines and can certainly be considered a wonder of modern engineering. They are made up of thousands of different components. The structure of a modern airplane can be roughly divided into three main parts: the fuselage, the wingsand the tail. The fuselage can be described as a sort of "hollow tube" which accommodates the airplane passengers, its crewand the cargo. The fuselage is pressurised in order to allow the passengers and the crew to breathe normally during the flight. It has to be light and extremely sturdy, in order to withstand the stress of the flight and to ensure the airplane safety. The fuselage also hosts most of the airplane instrumentation, as well as the hydraulic systems and the electrical wiring. The wings are the components that really allow the airplane to fly. Thanks to them, the airplane can become airborne; in addition to this, by extending or retracting special surfaces called "flaps" and "slats", pilots can manage takeoffs and landings. The airplane engines are often attached to the wings; usually, an airplane can have two or four engines. The tail section of a plane is extremely important: on the tail there is the rudder, that allows pilots to control the airplane. The tail also plays a very important role in the aerodynamics of the flight. Last but not least, the landing gear supports the airplane when it is parked on the airport runway and when it is taking off or landing. The next time you board an airplaneplease take a minute to think of the marvellous machine you are going to be on, and enjoy your flight!

<input>Hi Harry,

Great to see you stepping into your new role! Motivating a team effectively takes more than just assigning tasks—it’s about creating an environment where people feel valued, supported, and inspired to grow.

Start by building trust. Take the time to listen to your team members and involve them in decisions when possible. When employees feel heard and respected, they’re much more likely to stay motivated. All the best in your new position!
Kashish Chhabra</input>

<input>When I was a kid, I would frequently go to my grandparents' house in the Portuguese countryside, to a village called Benedita. I keep many memories from that time, one of them being my grandmother trying to put me and my sister to bed, waiting for us to fall asleep. In those moments, she would talk to us about "João Pestana" ("John Eyelash," in a literal English translation). The way my grandmother used to say, "Let's go to bed, because João Pestana must be arriving soon!" in such a tender voice, left me with no doubt about the good nature of this man.

And now that I am a grown-up woman, with some research done about this fictional character, I can say that I was right: João Pestana is indeed a shy and calm Portuguese mythical figure of sleep that only comes when everything is deeply silent. He may be compared to the well-known "Sandman" in other Anglo-Saxon cultures. At the moment he arrives, children close their eyelashes (hence the name) and fall into a deep sleep. That's why no one has ever seen him.

In Portugal, we have many songs (lullabies) and popular poems about João Pestana. To my grandmother, a big thank you for having brought them to me. Coincidence or not, I’ve always had an easy and very good sleep.

See you soon, João Pestana!</input>
